chapters.title: David mourns Saul and Jonathan

parts.text: An Amalekite arrives at Ziklag with Saul’s crown and bracelet, reporting Israel’s defeat and the deaths of Saul and Jonathan. He claims that he killed Saul at the wounded king’s request. David and his men mourn and fast. David condemns the messenger for claiming to destroy the LORD’s anointed and orders his execution, saying his own testimony has condemned him.

David composes a lament for Saul and Jonathan and orders it taught in Judah. He grieves over the mighty fallen on Gilboa, asks that the news not become Philistine triumph, and recalls the strength and companionship of the dead. His words honour Saul’s benefits to Israel and express his particular anguish for Jonathan, whose love had been exceptionally precious to him.

chapters.title: David rules Judah while Israel follows Ish-bosheth

parts.text: Seeking the LORD’s guidance, David moves with his household and men to Hebron. Judah anoints him king. He thanks Jabesh-gilead for burying Saul and urges courage. Meanwhile Abner establishes Saul’s son Ish-bosheth as king over the other tribes from Mahanaim. David reigns in Hebron over Judah for seven years and six months.

Abner’s forces and David’s men under Joab meet at Gibeon. A contest turns into battle, and David’s side prevails. Joab’s swift brother Asahel pursues Abner, refusing repeated warnings to turn aside, until Abner kills him. Joab and Abishai continue the pursuit. At Abner’s appeal, Joab sounds the trumpet and ends the fighting. Both sides count their losses and return home.

chapters.title: Abner seeks unity but Joab murders him

parts.text: The war between Saul’s house and David’s continues, with David growing stronger. After Ish-bosheth accuses Abner concerning Saul’s concubine, Abner resolves to transfer the kingdom to David. David requires the return of Michal, and she is taken from her husband. Abner persuades Israel’s elders to recognize David and visits him at Hebron, receiving a peaceful welcome and an agreement to gather the nation.

Joab returns, condemns David’s dealings with Abner, and secretly summons him back. He kills Abner in revenge for Asahel. David declares his own innocence, pronounces judgment upon Joab’s house, and publicly mourns Abner. His lament and refusal to eat convince the people that he did not authorize the murder. He acknowledges Abner’s greatness and entrusts judgment to the LORD.

chapters.title: Ish-bosheth is murdered

parts.text: After Abner’s death, Ish-bosheth loses courage and Israel is troubled. The chapter identifies two Benjamite captains, Baanah and Rechab, and also explains how Jonathan’s young son Mephibosheth became lame during the panic following Saul’s death. The captains enter Ish-bosheth’s house while he rests, murder him on his bed, and take his head.

They bring the head to David in Hebron, claiming that the LORD has avenged him on Saul’s household. David rejects their interpretation and recalls executing the man who reported Saul’s death as good news. How much more, he says, must wicked men answer for killing an innocent man in his own house. He orders their execution, while Ish-bosheth’s head is buried honourably in Abner’s sepulchre.

chapters.title: David becomes king over all Israel and takes Jerusalem

parts.text: Israel’s tribes come to David at Hebron, acknowledging their kinship and his earlier leadership. They make a covenant with him and anoint him king over all Israel. David captures the Jebusite stronghold of Zion and makes Jerusalem his city. Hiram of Tyre supplies materials and workers for a palace. David recognizes that the LORD has established his kingdom for Israel’s sake, and his household grows.

The Philistines attack after hearing of David’s anointing. David twice seeks the LORD’s direction. First he receives permission to attack and defeats them at Baal-perazim. When they return, God prescribes a different approach around the mulberry trees, with the sound of marching as the signal. David obeys and wins another victory.

chapters.title: The ark comes to Jerusalem

parts.text: David gathers Israel to bring the ark from Abinadab’s house on a new cart, accompanied by celebration. When the oxen shake it, Uzzah reaches out to steady it, and God strikes him dead. David is displeased and afraid, naming the place Perez-uzzah. He leaves the ark with Obed-edom for three months, during which the LORD blesses that household.

Hearing of the blessing, David brings the ark to Jerusalem with sacrifices, shouting, trumpets, and dancing before the LORD. He places it in the prepared tent, blesses the people, and distributes food. Michal despises his public celebration and reproaches him. David answers that he rejoiced before the LORD who chose him above her father’s house. Michal remains childless until her death.

chapters.title: God promises David an enduring house

parts.text: David wishes to build a house for the ark rather than leave it in curtains while he lives in cedar. Through Nathan, God recalls that he never required such a house during Israel’s journeys and that he raised David from tending sheep. He promises rest and an enduring house for David. David’s seed will build a house for God’s name, and his throne will be established. God will discipline wrongdoing but not withdraw mercy as he did from Saul.

David sits before the LORD in grateful wonder at this promise reaching beyond his own life. He praises God’s greatness and Israel’s redemption, acknowledges the truth of God’s words, and asks that the promised blessing upon his house be established forever.

chapters.title: David’s victories and administration

parts.text: David subdues the Philistines and defeats Moab, placing its survivors under tribute. He also defeats Hadadezer of Zobah and the Syrians who come to assist him, taking spoils and establishing garrisons. The LORD preserves David wherever he goes. Gold shields and much brass are brought back from the defeated territories.

Toi of Hamath sends gifts after David’s victory over their common enemy. David dedicates these and other spoils to the LORD. Further victories bring Edom under his authority through garrisons. The chapter then describes David ruling all Israel with judgment and justice and names his leading officers, including Joab over the army, Jehoshaphat as recorder, the priests, the scribe, and Benaiah over the royal guard.

chapters.title: David shows kindness to Mephibosheth

parts.text: David asks whether anyone remains of Saul’s house to whom he may show kindness for Jonathan’s sake. Ziba tells him about Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet and living in Lo-debar. David summons him. The fearful man bows before the king, but David assures him that he will restore Saul’s land and give him a permanent place at the royal table.

David directs Ziba, his sons, and servants to cultivate the land for Mephibosheth’s household, while Mephibosheth himself eats with the king like one of his sons. The chapter also names Mephibosheth’s son Micha. David’s provision establishes the surviving member of Jonathan’s household in Jerusalem despite his weakness and former family rivalry.

chapters.title: The Ammonites shame David’s messengers

parts.text: David sends condolences to Hanun after the death of his father, the Ammonite king, remembering former kindness. Hanun’s advisers accuse the visitors of spying. He humiliates them by shaving half their beards and cutting their garments, and David tells them to remain at Jericho until their beards grow. Recognizing the offence, Ammon hires Syrian forces and prepares for war.

Joab divides Israel’s army against the two fronts, placing Abishai against Ammon while he faces the Syrians, with each pledging support to the other. Both enemies retreat. Hadarezer then brings further Syrian forces, and David gathers Israel, crosses Jordan, and defeats them. The Syrian kings make peace and serve Israel, becoming afraid to assist Ammon again.

chapters.title: David’s sin with Bath-sheba and Uriah’s death

parts.text: While Joab besieges Rabbah, David remains in Jerusalem. He sees Bath-sheba bathing, learns that she is Uriah’s wife, sends for her, and lies with her. She later reports that she is pregnant. David summons Uriah from the army and tries to send him home, but Uriah refuses personal comforts while the ark and soldiers remain in the field. Even making him drunk does not change his resolve.

David sends Uriah back carrying an order to place him in deadly combat and withdraw support. Joab arranges the attack, and Uriah and other men die. David dismisses the loss as the fortunes of war. After Bath-sheba mourns, he takes her as wife and she bears a son. The chapter closes by declaring that David’s deed displeased the LORD.

chapters.title: Nathan confronts David and announces judgment

parts.text: Nathan tells David of a rich man who stole a poor man’s cherished lamb. When David angrily condemns the offender, Nathan declares that David is that man. God recounts his gifts to David and exposes the taking of Uriah’s wife and murder of Uriah. Violence and public humiliation will come upon David’s household. David confesses his sin, and Nathan announces forgiveness but also the child’s impending death.

David fasts and pleads while the child is sick. After the child dies, he worships and resumes eating, explaining that he cannot bring him back. Bath-sheba later bears Solomon, whom the LORD loves and names Jedidiah through Nathan. Joab summons David to complete Rabbah’s capture, and David takes the city, its crown, and spoil, imposing severe judgment upon the Ammonite cities.

chapters.title: Amnon assaults Tamar and Absalom takes revenge

parts.text: Amnon desires his half-sister Tamar. Following Jonadab’s scheme, he feigns illness and asks David to send her to prepare food. Once alone with her, he overpowers and rapes her despite her pleas. His desire turns to hatred, and he has her expelled. Tamar tears her garment, mourns, and remains desolate in Absalom’s house. David is very angry, while Absalom conceals his hatred of Amnon.

Two years later, Absalom invites the king’s sons to sheep-shearing and orders his servants to kill Amnon when he is drinking. The other princes flee, and a false report initially says all are dead. Jonadab explains that only Amnon has been targeted. Absalom escapes to Geshur for three years, while David mourns and eventually longs toward him.

chapters.title: Absalom returns but remains estranged

parts.text: Joab arranges for a wise woman from Tekoah to present David with a supposed case: one son has killed another, and relatives want to execute the survivor, extinguishing the family. After obtaining David’s promise of protection, she applies the appeal to his failure to restore his own banished son. David recognizes Joab’s involvement, and she admits it.

David permits Absalom to return to Jerusalem but forbids him from seeing the king. The chapter describes Absalom’s striking appearance, heavy hair, and children. After two years without an audience, he repeatedly summons Joab and finally burns his barley field to force attention. Joab conveys Absalom’s demand to be received or judged. David summons Absalom, who bows before him, and the king kisses him.

chapters.title: Absalom’s rebellion drives David from Jerusalem

parts.text: Absalom builds a public following with chariots, runners, and personal attention to those seeking justice. He suggests that he would give them fair hearings and gradually steals Israel’s hearts. Under the pretext of fulfilling a vow, he goes to Hebron, sends agents to proclaim him king, and gathers supporters, including Ahithophel. The conspiracy grows strong.

David flees Jerusalem to spare the city attack. Loyal servants and Ittai’s men accompany him. He sends the ark back with Zadok and Abiathar, entrusting his future to God and arranging communication through their sons. Weeping as he climbs Olivet, David prays that Ahithophel’s counsel be frustrated. He sends Hushai back to undermine that counsel while Absalom enters Jerusalem.

chapters.title: Ziba’s accusation, Shimei’s curses, and Absalom’s counsel

parts.text: Ziba brings David provisions and accuses Mephibosheth of remaining in Jerusalem in hope of recovering Saul’s kingdom. David grants him Mephibosheth’s property. Shimei, from Saul’s family, curses David and throws stones, blaming him for Saul’s blood. David restrains Abishai from killing him, allowing that the LORD may have permitted the affliction and may turn it to good.

In Jerusalem, Hushai presents himself to Absalom and professes allegiance to the chosen ruler. Absalom asks Ahithophel’s advice. He recommends publicly taking David’s concubines to make the breach with his father unmistakable and strengthen the rebels’ resolve. Absalom does so in a tent on the roof. The chapter notes the extraordinary authority Ahithophel’s counsel held with both David and Absalom.

chapters.title: Hushai frustrates Ahithophel’s plan

parts.text: Ahithophel advises an immediate attack with a selected force while David is weary, aiming to kill only the king and recover the people. Hushai argues instead for gathering all Israel under Absalom’s personal leadership, warning that David is an experienced and dangerous fighter. Absalom and the elders prefer Hushai’s advice. The account states that the LORD appointed this to defeat Ahithophel’s good counsel and bring harm upon Absalom.

Hushai sends warning through the priests’ sons, who escape detection with a woman’s help and reach David. His company crosses Jordan before morning. Ahithophel, seeing his advice rejected, arranges his household and hangs himself. Absalom appoints Amasa over the army and crosses Jordan, while supporters bring generous provisions to David’s weary followers at Mahanaim.

chapters.title: Absalom dies and David mourns

parts.text: David organizes his army under Joab, Abishai, and Ittai but stays in the city at the people’s urging. He publicly commands gentle treatment of Absalom. David’s forces win in the wood of Ephraim, where the terrain contributes heavily to the losses. Absalom becomes caught by his head in an oak while his mule runs on. Despite the king’s order, Joab strikes him, and his armourbearers kill him. Absalom is buried beneath a heap of stones.

Ahimaaz and Cushi run with news. David anxiously asks whether Absalom is safe. Ahimaaz avoids a clear answer, but Cushi’s response reveals the death. The king withdraws in anguish, repeatedly crying for his son and wishing he had died in Absalom’s place.

chapters.title: David returns amid mercy and renewed division

parts.text: David’s grief over Absalom turns victory into shame for his followers. Joab sharply warns that unless he encourages them, they will desert him. David takes his place publicly, and discussions begin about restoring him. He appeals to Judah’s kinship and offers Amasa Joab’s command, winning Judah’s support for bringing him back across Jordan.

Shimei pleads for pardon, which David grants against Abishai’s objections. Mephibosheth explains that Ziba deceived and slandered him; David orders the land divided, and Mephibosheth welcomes his return above property. Barzillai declines court life because of age but sends Chimham. As David returns, the other tribes resent Judah’s dominant role, and a bitter argument exposes continuing divisions within the restored kingdom.

chapters.title: Sheba’s revolt and Joab’s return to command

parts.text: Sheba, a Benjamite, calls Israel away from David, while Judah remains loyal. David confines the concubines left in Jerusalem to protected widowhood. He orders Amasa to gather forces, but delay leads him to send Abishai after Sheba. Joab meets Amasa, greets him deceptively, and kills him with a sword. Once Amasa’s body is removed from the road, the troops follow Joab.

Sheba takes refuge in Abel of Beth-maachah, which Joab besieges. A wise woman asks why he seeks to destroy a peaceable city and learns that he wants only Sheba. She persuades the inhabitants, and Sheba’s head is thrown over the wall. Joab withdraws, ending the revolt. The chapter closes with the chief officers of David’s government.

chapters.title: Saul’s bloodguilt and battles with giants

parts.text: A three-year famine leads David to inquire of the LORD, who identifies Saul’s violence against the Gibeonites as its cause. The Gibeonites request seven of Saul’s descendants for execution. David spares Jonathan’s son because of their oath but delivers seven others. Rizpah guards the exposed bodies from birds and beasts. Moved by this devotion, David gathers their remains with Saul’s and Jonathan’s bones for burial. Afterward God responds to the land’s need.

Further Philistine wars include an attack in which a giant threatens the weary David, and Abishai saves him. David’s men then forbid him from returning to battle. Other warriors kill additional descendants of the giant, whose names and unusual size or weaponry are recorded.

chapters.title: David praises his deliverer

parts.text: David sings to the LORD after deliverance from his enemies and Saul. He calls God his rock, fortress, shield, and refuge. He recalls mortal danger and his cry for help, describing God’s response through powerful images of earthquake, storm, darkness, thunder, and rescue from deep waters. David says the LORD brought him into a broad place and rewarded him according to his righteousness and faithfulness.

The song declares that God deals faithfully with the faithful, humbles pride, lights darkness, and strengthens his servant for battle. David credits God with victory over enemies and authority among nations, whose peoples submit to him. He praises the living LORD and promises thanksgiving among the heathen, ending with God’s great deliverance and mercy toward his anointed, David and his seed forever.

chapters.title: David’s final words and mighty men

parts.text: David’s last words describe him as the man raised up and anointed by God. He says the LORD’s Spirit spoke through him, declaring that a ruler must be just and govern in the fear of God, bringing blessing like clear morning light and rain-fed growth. David rests in God’s everlasting, ordered covenant with him, while the worthless are pictured as thorns destined for burning.

The chapter records David’s mighty men and their remarkable deeds, repeatedly crediting the LORD with victory. Three warriors risk their lives to bring him water from Beth-lehem, which he pours out to God rather than drink at such a cost. Abishai and Benaiah receive particular notice. A larger roll of warriors follows, ending with Uriah the Hittite and a total of thirty-seven.

chapters.title: David’s census and the plague

parts.text: The LORD’s anger is kindled against Israel, and David orders a census despite Joab’s objection. After the count is completed, David’s heart smites him, and he confesses that he has sinned foolishly. Through Gad, God offers three forms of judgment: famine, flight before enemies, or pestilence. David chooses to fall into the LORD’s hands, trusting his great mercy rather than human mercy.

A plague kills seventy thousand. As the destroying angel reaches Jerusalem, God stops him at Araunah’s threshingfloor. David pleads for the people and, following Gad’s direction, buys the site and animals rather than offering God what costs him nothing. He builds an altar and offers burnt and peace offerings. The LORD answers for the land, and the plague is stayed.
